pr_body:
Fixes #6458.

`options.entryRoot` is used during naming as a common root directory from which to determine relative paths for non-hashed bundles. However, this is computed before entry resolution, so if an entry resolves to a directory, the computed root will be wrong. In addition, if entries have different targets, it will also be incorrect. This PR replaces this with a `bundleGraph.getEntryRoot` method, which receives a target, finds all of the entries associated with that target distDir, and computes the common root dir from there. This is memoized per target dist dir for performance.

In addition, it seems we were exposing internal bundle group objects with project paths instead of full file paths. This adds a public wrapper class for bundle groups like we have for all of our other public objects.

issue_context.title: Wrong distDir when using `parcel watch .`
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

The output of `parcel watch .` ends up in the wrong directory.

## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

```json
// package.json
{
  "private": true,
  "targets": {
    "default": {
      "context": "browser",
      "source": "src/index.html",
      "distDir": "public"
    }
  },
  "scripts": {
    "watch": "parcel watch ."
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "parcel": "^2.0.0-beta.3.1"
  }
}
```

The only other file I have is `src/index.html`.

![bilde](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/464152/122064336-5e6dd200-cdf1-11eb-9e64-1fc66076ab55.png)

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

I want parcel to build and produce `public/index.html`. 

## 😯 Current Behavior

When I run this the file ends up in `public/<parent-folder-name>/src/index.html`. In the image below (and above) the project is in the folder `parcel-test`, which is why the build output is in `public/parcel-test/index.html`. 

![bilde](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/464152/122064027-177fdc80-cdf1-11eb-814d-229e9c6a74f7.png)

## 💻 Code Sample

There's not much more than the `package.json` file in this scenario, just an html file with the default content from vscode snippet `html:5`:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="IE=edge">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Document</title>
</head>
<body>

</body>
</html>
```

## 🌍 Your Environment

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           | 2.0.0-beta.3.1 |
| Node             | 14.16.1 |
| npm/Yarn         | 6.14.12 |
| Operating System | Windows 10 |

<!-- Love parcel? Please consider supporting our collective:
👉  https://opencollective.com/parcel/donate -->
comments:
In your package.json you need the following:
```
"web": "public/index.html",
"targets": {
    "web": {
        "context": "browser",
        "publicUrl": "./"
    }
},
```

and your build script should be `parcel build ./src/index.html --target web`

You can replace `web` with anything you want (As long as it is not an already defined target)
What if I have several html pages, do I need to specify a target for each one of them?

And why is this necessary to configure? It seems like a weird default to include the parent folder name in the path. What's the reason for doing so? When is that the expected output? 
I think you may be looking for this documentation: [Specifying entrypoints](https://v2.parceljs.org/getting-started/configuration/#specifying-entrypoints)

So you could define your script to be: `parcel watch './src/*.html' --target web`
and you package.json to have:
```
"web": "public/index.html",
"targets": {
    "web": {
        "context": "browser",
        "publicUrl": "./"
    }
},
```

As for your other questions, I dont know. Would be interested to find out if someone else can answer
_Note: the above has not been tested, just going off what I know/read and hopfully it can help you get going_
